name: under-brace
title: Under Brace
description: A regex tester that annotates matches beneath the sample text with box-drawing braces instead of inline highlight color: each match gets its own └──┘ span, and capture groups add further rows stepped by nesting depth, the group's number printed inside its brace. A live, aria-live match list backs the same data for assistive tech; hovering a brace or a group chip lights every span it touches, and an invalid pattern prints the engine's own error under a ┗ caret pointer.
useWhen: testing or debugging a regular expression against real sample text, where seeing WHICH characters a match and its capture groups actually gripped — including how groups nest inside each other — matters more than a pass/fail verdict. Pick diagram-ascii-flow instead for a supplied graph rendered as a static, draggable box-drawing diagram (no text, no pattern matching); pick validation-inline-wick instead for a single form field's pass/fail state, an eased color diffusion from one offending character with no structural, multi-row annotation.
instruction: A regex tester (pattern input, flags input, sample <textarea>) whose result is rendered as box-drawing braces stacked BENEATH the sample text rather than inline highlight color — the five-token palette (--background --foreground --ns-muted --border --ns-accent) has no room for one hue per capture group, so depth is read from vertical position and opacity instead. MATCHING: the pattern is compiled with `new RegExp(pattern, 'gd' + sanitizedFlags)` — 'g' and 'd' (match indices) are always forced on internally regardless of what the user types in the flags field, which only accepts i/m/s; `sample.matchAll(regex)` then walks every match, and each participating capture group's exact [start,end) comes straight from `match.indices[n]`, never re-derived from string search. ROW ASSIGNMENT (the actual mechanic): `analyzePattern` walks the PATTERN SOURCE once — tracking character-class state, backslash escapes, and a stack of open groups — to assign every capturing group a fixed depth: a plain `(` or named `(?<x>` opens a numbered capturing group at (enclosing capturing depth + 1); `(?:`, `(?=`, `(?!`, `(?<=`, `(?<!` open a non-capturing construct whose CONTENTS still nest but which itself never gets a number or a row. Row 0, immediately under the text, is always reserved for the whole match's own brace; a capturing group at source depth 1 renders on row 1, depth 2 on row 2, and so on, clamped at 4 so a pathologically nested pattern still renders instead of growing without bound. Because the depth comes from the pattern's own text, a group's row is stable pattern-to-pattern and never jumps around as the SAMPLE changes, only as the PATTERN's structure does. Each row's brace is built as one literal string of box-drawing characters — `└` + `─`×(width-2) + `┘` for anything 2+ columns wide, a lone `┴` for a single-column match, `│` for a genuine zero-length match — square corners deliberately, not the rounded ╰╯ set: they're the glyphs already proven, elsewhere in this registry (diagram-ascii-flow, container-box-drawing), to have a predictable 1ch advance in Geist Mono, which this component's whole column mapping depends on — with the group's number centered inside the dashes when there's room (width ≥ label.length + 2); the whole match's own row-0 brace never carries a number. Every brace is positioned with plain `ch` units against a true monospace font (Geist Mono) — one character of the sample line equals exactly 1ch in its own annotation row, so no pixel measurement or per-character span grid is needed, just `left: {col}ch` on one span holding the whole glyph run. A match or group whose span crosses a line break is clipped and rendered separately on every line it touches. REVEAL: each brace span carries a registered `--under-brace-reveal` custom property (`@property`, syntax `<percentage>`) driving its own `mask-image`, animated 0%→100% left-to-right over `max(120ms, min(600ms, width*12ms))` with an ease-out curve — width-proportional so a two-character brace and a twenty-character one both feel like the same reveal speed rather than the wide one snapping in. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes the mask and animation entirely so every brace is simply present at full width immediately — still fully legible and interactive, nothing to wait on. INTERACTION: hovering (or, via a group chip, focusing) a brace tints its EXACT covered substring in the annotated view using `color-mix(in srgb, var(--ns-accent) 18%, transparent)` — --ns-accent used only for this and the standard focus rings, never resting decoration. Because the live pattern <input>'s own text can't be individually decorated without breaking normal editing/selection/IME behavior, 'hovering a group token' is implemented as a small strip of real `<button aria-label="Group N">` chips rendered next to the pattern field, one per capturing group; hovering OR focusing a chip lights every brace with that group number across every match at once, tinting every one of that group's substrings simultaneously — the intended way to answer 'everywhere this group grabbed, across the whole sample'. INVALID PATTERNS: `new RegExp` is wrapped in try/catch; on failure the engine's own SyntaxError message renders verbatim below the field, and a caret position is approximated by shrinking the pattern from the end, one character at a time, until a PREFIX of it compiles standalone — exact for the single most common live-editing mistake (a dangling trailing construct, e.g. a second quantifier), honestly degrading to column 0 for a still-open group or class where no single column is really at fault; the caret renders as a `┗` glyph positioned the same `ch`-unit way as the braces themselves, under the pattern field rather than the sample. ACCESSIBILITY: the entire annotated brace block is one `aria-hidden` decorative layer; the real, assistive-tech-facing surface is the plain native pattern `<input>` (`aria-invalid` mirrors whether the current pattern fails to compile, `aria-describedby` always points at one paragraph carrying either the live match count, 'Type a pattern to test it.', or the SyntaxError text), the plain native sample `<textarea>` (fully untouched keyboard/IME/undo/selection behavior), and a 'Matches' `<ol aria-live="polite">` of real `<button>`s, one per match, each reading e.g. 'Match 1: "#TX-482" at 7–14; group 1: "TX-482"; group 2: "482"' — updating live on every pattern, flag, or sample edit. Tab reaches the pattern input, the flags input, every group chip, the sample textarea, and every match button in document order; focusing (Tab or click) a match button draws a visible `outline: 2px solid var(--ns-accent)` directly on that match's OWN row-0 brace in the annotated view, in addition to the button's own native focus ring, so keyboard users see the visible focus indicator land on the thing it refers to, not just on the list item naming it. No canvas, no SVG, no per-group hex — pure DOM text and CSS, and every color in the whole component resolves to one of the five tokens.
